notes.text: Source report: the page begins with (13), E identified with dot T×[0,1], and a commutative diagram fixing the copy of dot T at parameter zero. It then gives the product condition for a closed X prime to be called compatible with a cylindrical neighbourhood E of B. A marginal correction proposes “plutot : transversale !”. The later cylindrical/conical comparison is heavily revised, and the final paragraph removes finie from the family formulation. This report of content is not itself a mathematical proof.

Targeted proof check supplied by the main reader and rechecked here: restrict the given product collar h:E→B×[0,1] to E∩X prime. The stated compatibility condition identifies this restriction with B prime×[0,1]. Since h sends the embedded B to B×{0}, taking the zero slice gives (B∩X prime)×{0}=B prime×{0}, hence B prime=B∩X prime. Moreover, E∩X prime is a neighbourhood of B∩X prime in the subspace X prime because E is a neighbourhood of B in X. The restricted product identification therefore gives the claimed bord structure on B∩X prime inside X prime. Closedness of X prime implies that its intersection with B is closed in B. This is an actual product/restriction check, separate from reading the marginal words.

The source emphasizes that cylindrical “transversalité” “n’est pas” a special case of the conical comparison but “mais est” followed by the revised plus exigeant(e) clause. Its added condition is T prime∩Y=0.dot T prime. The exact earlier conical definition is not supplied afresh on this assigned leaf. No independent proof of the full cylindrical/conical comparison is claimed, and mathematical expectation does not resolve exigeante/exigeant, the pronoun before devait, or the struck terminal set-like group.

The initial decorated X has a clear upper prime and a second, low branched mark. The transcription keeps that second mark as a subscript with k/star/epsilon alternatives, with k preferred after root inspection; its use is not defined on this leaf. H’s editorial claim of an earlier X* does not establish a separately recoverable cancelled copy, so none is duplicated.

Two local overwriting layers are distinguished. In the product formula the thinner upper and lower B bowls remain under the heavy E arms, so deleted B followed by E is recorded. In the preceding prose E the B-like old body is less secure and remains doubtful. This is not a global change of font. In the later cancelled formula E is retraced but no preceding glyph is recoverable; no earlier T or other letter is supplied there.

The curved stroke under 0.dot T prime is continuous with the descending g of exigeant(e) above. It is not treated as an independent box or underline, despite H’s editorial “entouré”. Likewise, insertion leaders near fermée and compatibilité are separated from parentheses and cancellations. The live adjective and mais est are not duplicated into additional crossed passages.

Literal forms retained include bord rather than bordante, homéom. rather than its expansion, néc with raised t and a baseline stop, plutot without an independently visible circumflex, cônique with its visible arch over o, and de = as the written abbreviation for de même. The final grammar after deleting finie and de is left as written; no extra de is restored. The final verb is unaccented definit on the wider original view. The marginal bord/à bord junction and adjective endings now retain explicit local alternatives.

The diagram has three objects, two directed shafts, two terminal heads and one hook, plus two independent strokes of a vertical identification. These components were counted twice. The mid-diagonal notch is continuous with the closing parenthesis of (t,0); it is not reproduced as another arrowhead. No arrowhead is added to the vertical straight stroke.

Reading record: only this assigned page, its C/H packet, current notation, preamble and governing protocol were used. The original was viewed once, both prepared native halves once, and P00–P18 once each. P09 and P10 were rotated for their slanted notes; original boxes and rotations are saved. Root independently reviewed all 19 crops. No OCR, recognition library, outside research, compilation, other-page report or other-page image was used.

There is no author folio number visible at the head. The thin lower-left 16 is separately retained with uncertain hand attribution. The terminal stop after the long marginal note’s final X prime is not visible and is omitted; the final main-text family sentence does have its own distinct stop. Physical clipping at the right edge is not silently completed.

Main-reader conditional check of the comparison, using the full-ambient-ray interpretation distinguished on scan016: in a cylinder B×[0,1], a full-ray-saturated conical subset has the form S=(A×[0,1])∪(C×{0}), with A⊂C⊂B. Its outer slice is A×{1}, its base slice is C×{0}, and 0.dot S=A×{0}. Thus S∩B=0.dot S is exactly C=A, which is exactly the product condition S=A×[0,1] used by cylindrical compatibility. Taking A empty and C nonempty shows why conical compatibility allowing an extra base slice is weaker. This verification requires the stated full-ray reconstruction; it does not repair the insufficient literal conditions (12)a,b discussed on scan016.

Independent audit: root personally inspected all 19 nonidentical boxes, enlarged the de/la junction and slanted marginal junction, and checked the wider original bottom lines. Eleven boxes were revised. Alternative-only doubts retain their first preferred readings and do not generate new primary C corrections. All fixed first/second readings remain unchanged.
